visuals: Right triangle with labeled legs and hypotenuse
Squares constructed on each side to represent areas
logic_steps: Label the shorter legs as a and b

scenes.title: The Pythagorean Theorem
scenes.description: Introduce the topic with a clear, centered right triangle and the formula a² + b² = c² appearing below it.

scenes.title: Visualizing the Relationship
scenes.description: Animate squares growing out of each side of the triangle to show that the area of the legs equals the area of the hypotenuse.
visual_elements: Expanding squares on sides a, b, and c
Color-coded areas (green for legs, red for hypotenuse)

scenes.title: Worked Example: The 3-4-5 Triangle
scenes.description: Solve for the hypotenuse using a=3 and b=4. Show the substitution: 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25, so c = 5(25).

scenes.title: Key Takeaways
scenes.description: Recap the conditions: only works for right triangles, c is always the longest side, and it connects algebra to geometry.

visualization.primary_visual: Geometric construction of squares on a right triangle to prove area relationship

key_points: The hypotenuse (c) is always opposite the right angle
The sum of the squares of the legs equals the square of the hypotenuse
educational.emphasis: Visualizing the theorem through area comparison makes the abstract formula intuitive

scenes.title: The Approximation Problem
scenes.description: Introduce the challenge of calculating complex functions (e.g., sin(x), e^x) and the need for simple polynomial approximations.
visual_elements: Question mark overlay indicating the gap

scenes.title: Matching at a Point
scenes.description: Explain the core logic: to approximate f(x) at point a, the polynomial P(x) must match f(x) in value, slope, and curvature at a.
visual_elements: Zoomed in view of point 'a' on the curve
Parabola snapping to curve (2nd order match)

scenes.title: The Taylor Formula
scenes.description: Derive and display the general Taylor Series formula, explaining the role of factorials and powers of (x-a).

scenes.title: Visualizing Convergence
scenes.description: Demonstrate the approximation of e^x or sin(x) near x=0, showing how the error decreases as more terms are added.
visual_elements: Polynomials P1, P2, P3, P4 appearing sequentially
Graph diverging further from center point

scenes.title: Summary & Applications
scenes.description: Review key takeaways: local accuracy, infinite series potential, and use cases in calculators/physics.

visualization.primary_visual: Animated overlay of polynomial curves progressively fitting a target smooth function (e.g., sine or exponential) centered at x=0.

key_points: Taylor series turns calculus (derivatives) into algebra (polynomials)
Approximation is exact at the center point 'a'
Accuracy improves with more terms (higher degree)
educational.emphasis: Understanding that matching derivatives forces the polynomial to 'hug' the curve tighter at the expansion point.
